changes.reason: Fault fixed: all four values now carry U+2212 and U+00B0 (byte-checked) and are the same numbers as live (-3, 3, -2, -8 parse to -3, 3, -2, -8). Option ids, isKey (A) and all three tags match live; stem byte-identical; rebuild carries no explanation/lineRefs, so those stay as stored. solution '5 - 8' = -3 = key (evaluateSolution/optionNumericValue). Executions: B (maths-66, ignoring the minus or turning back at zero) gives 3, and 5 - 8 = -3 is right. C (maths-107) lands one step short toward zero: 8 steps down from 5 is -3, so -2 is one out. That is the tag's own direction (-4 for -5), though it does not name the zero-counted-as-a-step mechanism. D (maths-71, a given number never used) leaves out the 5 and counts 8 down from zero, giving -8; 5 - 8 = -3 is right. Every number checked.

rows.reason: Notation is now uniform, so the form (sign or degree mark) no longer gives the key away, and the key -3°C is the only correct option. But the VALUE pattern gives it away: the key is the only option linked to two others. 3°C is its sign twin and -2°C is one step from it. -8°C is linked to nothing. A child can pick the hub without working out 5 - 8. It is also the brief's named pattern: two options one apart, with the key the smaller (-3 and -2), and it is the same on the only other row built this way (MC05-NPV-06). The pattern was not introduced by this rebuild. It was on the live row already, and the notation fix is correct. Repair: redraft one distractor so the key is not the only option linked to two others.
